newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan 1997 exports, imports seen up 8.0, 5.6 pct.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan 1997 exports, imports seen up 8.0, 5.6 pct.

text.p: Taiwan's finance ministry expected the island's exports and imports in 1997 to grow 8.0 percent and 5.6 percent respectively, from 1996, the local Economic Daily News reported on Thursday.

The newspaper quoted the ministry's statistics department head Hsu Kuo-chung as saying that exports and imports should have modest growth in 1997 due to expected stable growth in the international economy.

If the government could speed up infrastructure projects, Taiwan should be able to reach the government;s November forecast of 6.2 percent gross domestic product growth for 1997, the paper quoted Hsu as saying.
The ministry also estimated that the island's 1996 exports rose 3.8 percent from 1995 to US$115.6 billion, but imports fell 1.0 percent from 1995 to US$102.3 billion, the paper said.
Taiwan's trade surplus in 1996 was estimated at US$13.3 billion, up 64 percent from 1995, the highest annual growth since 1985, the paper said.
The ministry attributed the 1996 imports decline to weak domestic demand in a slowing economy, it said.
Officials were not available for comment due to a national holiday.
The ministry was scheduled to release the actual December and full 1996 trade figures on January 7.
The reported forecasts for 1997 were slightly different from recent central bank predictions.
On Tuesday, the central bank, in a year-end press conference, projected that Taiwan could expect 1997 exports to grow 8.39 percent and imports to rise 7.34 percent from 1996.
